hook: A large white dog lies under a tree and attacks anyone who comes near the figure hanging from it. The article is short and mostly procedural, but it is less about a monster than about a bond that has outlasted everything else. A heads-up: the central image involves a death by hanging, described in clinical terms.
whyItMatters:
This is a good example of an entry where the anomaly is a relationship between two numbered parts rather than a single object. Everything the Foundation measures, from the dog's size and glow to the figure's movement, is described as depending on the distance between them.

It also shows a common Foundation pattern: after costly attempts to remove the threat, the decision is simply to leave it alone and keep people away.
thingsToNotice:
Watch how the description keeps falling back on proportional language: the closer the dog is to the hanged man, the bigger, brighter and stronger it gets, and the harder he jerks and gasps. That dry wording pays off in the first incident log. When the dog chases a fleeing agent out to 900 m, the hanging figure goes completely still, and the dog stops, looks back, howls once and runs home, after which the twitching starts again.

The second log reframes the whole file. As a D-class gets within 50 m, the hanged man slows, opens his eyes, lifts his arms toward the stranger as if to greet him, and seems to mouth "no, down boy" just before the dog kills the man anyway. Put that beside the single word on the collar tag: the dog is still guarding its owner from people he would have welcomed, and its loyalty is also what keeps him suspended in the middle of dying.
